# **![mozio\_logo\_320.png][image1]**

# **MOZIO API v2 INTEGRATION GUIDE**

Hello, and thank you for choosing Mozio as your ground transportation technology partner. After you integrate our API, you will have instant access to all Shuttles, Limos, Taxis, Airporters, Buses, Trains and all other transportation options available on our platform. Before production access, we run a quick certification process that takes less than a day, after which we provide your production keys.

This document aims to help you understand how our API works and how to connect and interact with it, giving you a brief overview of the API (architecture, authentication, localization support and more), a general step-by-step integration flow description and details (with examples) of each of those steps.

# OVERVIEW {#overview}

---

Mozio API has been designed using a [RESTful](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_State_Transfer) architecture, that relies on predictable, resource-oriented URLs, and HTTP response codes to indicate errors. It uses built-in HTTP features, like HTTP authentication and HTTP verbs, supported by most HTTP clients.

[JSON](http://www.json.org/) is returned by all API responses, including errors. You will need to make sure the appropriate *Content-Type* is present in your HTTP requests (i.e *application/json*).

| Heads up: For the sake of simplicity, in all sample requests/responses we will omit the `Content-Type` header since we will always use data in JSON format. |
| :---- |

To start **developing** and **testing**, you can point your requests to [https://api-testing.mozio.com](https://api-testing.mozio.com).  
When you are ready to move to **production**, use [https://api.mozio.com](https://api.mozio.com).

Regardless of the environment, note that **HTTPS** **is required**. Any request not using HTTPS will be ignored.

Also note that our current **API version** is 2, and all endpoints described in this document will begin with `/v2/`.

### AUTHENTICATION {#authentication}

For all of the resources in our API, you will also be **required** to have a valid **Mozio API key**.  
You need to send it as a header, called *API-KEY*. If the API key is required and is not provided, the API will return a HTTP 403 response.

| EXAMPLE: sending API requests with Mozio API key  `GET /v2/some_resource API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey>` |
| :---- |
| `HTTP/1.1 200 OK {   "response": "OK"  }` |

In case you don’t have API keys, please contact the Mozio team to get them for you.

### LOCALIZATION[^1] {#localization}

Our API supports localization to over 30 languages by adding an optional *LANG* header. The expected value must use the [IETF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) format.

Some of the supported languages include:

* English (en-US, default value)  
* Spanish (es-ES)  
* French (fr-FR)  
* German (de-DE)  
* Portuguese (pt-BR)

Note that only human-readable texts will be localized, meaning that the URLs or the name of the parameters or objects in responses won’t.

| EXAMPLE: sending API requests and expecting responses in another language  `GET /v2/some_resource/ API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey> LANG: es-ES` |
| :---- |
| `HTTP/1.1 200 OK {   "response": "¡Bienvenido!" }` |

### PAYMENTS AND CREDIT CARD DATA {#payments-and-credit-card-data}

Note that **no raw credit card information** is collected by our API during booking, nor any other process for that matter: credit card details are captured securely by the application and are never sent to our servers; we only capture secure, random tokens to identify the transaction that are generated by one of our payments processor’s client libraries.

### Payment management

There are a few different ways to handle payment through the API:

1. You manage payment data and handle the payment flow on your end, meaning you collect payments directly. We will issue an invoice in the following month for the total amount of bookings made. There is no additional information to be sent to the API.  
2. If you handle customer payment data, are PCI compliant and can provide the required documentation for it, you can use one of Stripe’s client libraries along with credentials provided by Mozio. This setup will allow your application to securely create tokens (see: [https://stripe.com/docs/api/tokens](https://stripe.com/docs/api/tokens)) that can be sent to the Mozio API. Using this method, you transmit payment information directly to Stripe, and only the token ID referencing this payment information needs to be passed to the Mozio API.

The following diagram explains the process:  
![][image2]

3. If you don't have access to the customer's payment data, Mozio will generate a Stripe payment page once the reservation is submitted, returning the page URL in the API response. You will need to redirect your customer to this page, where they can securely enter their payment information. After completing the payment, the customer will be redirected to a success page (which you must create) containing the `search_id`, it can be both path or query params. On this success page, you should continuously poll the reservation status using this `search_id` to retrieve the booking details and show it to the customer.  
   The following diagram explains the process![][image3]

### ERROR HANDLING {#error-handling}

For most of the API responses, errors will probably come in 2 major categories: authentication errors (HTTP 403), most likely due to missing or invalid API key, and bad requests errors (HTTP 400\) due to malformed inputs.

For bad requests, the JSON object returned will include all fields that were malformed during the request. For each of them you will receive a list of a 3-tuple structure containing a **code** (to categorize the error), a **message** (targeted at developers) and **user\_message** (targeted at end-users, which can be null).

When the errors are not related to a specific param but to all data instead, most likely due to global validation issues, a list of the same 3-tuple structure will be available inside a special object called **non\_field\_errors**.

If you ever encounter an error that you cannot debug yourself and need assistance, please contact the Mozio Tech team and include this error structure as part of your debugging request.

| EXAMPLE: sending a bad API request that raises a specific-param error  `GET /v2/some_resource/ API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey>` |
| :---- |
| `HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request {   "specific_param": [     {       "code": "required",       "message": "This field is required.",       "user_message": "You must send this param"     }   ] }` |

| EXAMPLE: sending a bad API request that raises a global validation error  `GET /v2/some_resource/ API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey>` |
| :---- |
| `HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request {   "specific_param": [     {       "code": "missing_currency",       "message": "You must provide a price_currency param.",       "user_message": "Ooops, you didn’t choose a currency."     }   ] }` |

# INTEGRATION FLOW {#integration-flow}

---

![][image4]

In general terms, the integration flow can be summarized as a 3-step process:

1. Searching  
2. Booking  
3. Cancellation

### SEARCHING {#searching}

Searching refers to the process of giving some basic inputs describing the intended trip –the start and end locations (e.g. JFK Airport to The Waldorf Astoria Hotel), the desired pickup time (e.g. April 15th, 3:30 PM) and the number of passengers, and receiving back quotes that fulfil that trip.

In case you don’t know the desired pickup time, our API can also calculate an estimated pickup time using flight data (time, if domestic or international, and airline / flight number). For domestic flight, we will calculate the pickup time for a transfer from the airport by adding 30 minutes to the flight datetime. If it’s international flight, we will add 60 minutes.

Since our API has to compose a list of quotes (using our in-house ground providers platform), and also query our network of external providers’ APIs for quotes in real-time, not all quotes can be returned immediately –it’s a dynamic process that inherently adds some delay. Therefore, the search process is composed by 2 subprocesses: **search request** and **search polling**.

Search request, as the name implies, refers to the process of letting the API know to begin a new search process.

Search polling is about the process of asking the API, every few seconds, about the results of that search. Each time you poll for search results, new quotes are returned (the list of quotes is dynamic –i.e. **poll results are not accumulable**). You can poll until no more search results are expected back.

At then end, each quote will have all data describing the offered trip, in general: the provider fulfilling the service, the type of vehicle to expect, any restrictions that may apply (maximum number of passengers and luggage allowed, schedules, boarding points, etc.), and total price for all passengers.

### BOOKING {#booking}

After you have a list of quotes and your user chooses one of them, booking refers to the process of requesting our external provider to secure and fulfil that trip described by the quote from search results.

Additionally to data from the quote, you will be required to pass all contact details from the passengers: names, email addresses, phone number and flight data (if relevant). Passengers are also able to send special instructions to providers, if supported by them (e.g. “Please announce yourself in the lobby” or “Please text me, my doorbell is broken”).

Similar to searches, the booking process is divided in **booking request** and **booking polling**. As before, the idea is to first place the request for a reservation, and then, start polling while our API connects to the provider’s API and receives a response.

After a reservation is placed successfully, our API will return a **confirmation number** that can be used for any further API requests, and any Customer Support as needed by the passenger. Contact details from the provider will be included as well. The passenger himself will receive a confirmation email with details about the reservation and what to do next to meet the driver or board the vehicle.

### CANCELLATION {#cancellation}

This process allows passengers to cancel an existing reservation and receive a full refund. However, not all reservations are cancellable: all quotes have a **cancellation policy** describing whether the trip is cancellable or not, and how many hours of notice are given to be entitled to a 100% refund.

Our API requires the confirmation number of the reservation to proceed with a cancellation. Keep in mind that this operation cannot be undone and that refunds may take up to 5 business days to be issued by our payments processor.

After a successful cancellation is made, the passenger will receive an email notification confirming the operation.

# SEARCHING {#searching-1}

---

### STARTING THE PROCESS {#starting-the-process}

**Endpoint**: `/v2/search/`  
**Allowed methods**: `POST`

**Highlights:**

* You can choose to either send the locations’ addresses or gps coordinates. For an airport, send the airports’ IATA code (e.g. JFK), and for other types of locations please try to provide as much data as you can. Mozio’s API uses Google Maps API, so you can also send the `place_id` from a given Google Maps API location.  
* Please provide the `pickup_datetime` when possible. If you cannot and your search is to or from an airport, you may use `flight_datetime` and our API will calculate an estimated pickup time for it. By default we consider the flight as international you can send `flight_type` as `domestic` otherwise:  
  * For Airport pickups we add 30 minutes buffer for domestic and 1 hour for international flights  
  * For Airport drop-offs we add 2 hours 30 minutes buffer for domestic and 3 hours 30 minutes for international flights

* If you don’t provide either `pickup_datetime` or `flight_datetime`, the pickup time will be set to 5 minutes from now.  
* If you need to perform a round-trip search (`mode` \= `round_trip`), don’t forget to provide either `return_flight_datetime` or `return_pickup_datetime`  
* To differentiate searches from different sources on your platform, you can pass us the `campaign` and `branch` parameters. Campaign is meant to identify major different sources of traffic, like “confirmation\_email” or “cross-sell-email”, while branch is meant to help differentiate things within the campaign itself such as different email creative. Keep in mind that it is okay to send a campaign but no branch, but sending a branch without a campaign is not allowed.  
* **Important:** Our API allows 100 search requests per minute in the production environment, after that the requests will be throttled. If you expect to have higher volume, please reach out and we can increase the limit. In the testing environment , our API allows 30 search requests per minute;  
* **Important:** Mozio searches are valid for 20 minutes. If you try to book after that time, we cannot guarantee that the pricing and availability will remain the same, and your booking attempt may fail (search\_expired error). To prevent this, please perform a new search to obtain the most up-to-date results.


| EXAMPLE: starting a search (note the empty `results` since polling is expected)  `POST /v2/search/ API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey> {   "start_address": "433 Park Ave, New York",   "end_address": "JFK",   "mode": "one_way",   "pickup_datetime": "2017-08-16 15:30",   "num_passengers": 2,   "currency": "USD",   “campaign”: “confirmation_email”,   “branch”: “version_a”, }` |
| :---- |
| `HTTP/1.1 201 Created {   "created_at": 1492730991,   "currency_info": {     "code": "USD",     "prefix_symbol": "$",     "suffix_symbol": ""   },   "end_location": {     "formatted_address": "John F Kennedy International Airport",     "full_address": "John F Kennedy International Airport",     "iata_code": "JFK",     "icao_code": "KJFK",     "lat": 40.639751,     "lng": -73.778926,     "place_id": "",     "timezone": "America/New_York"   },   "expires_at": 1492731891,   "flight_datetime": null,   "flight_type": "domestic",   "more_coming": true,   "num_passengers": 2,   "pickup_datetime": "2017-08-16T15:30:00-04:00",   "results": [],   "search_id": "5c8563a5d31d4c33a3a1eafbbfe59c4b",   "start_location": {     "formatted_address": "433 Park Ave, New York, NY 10022, USA",     "full_address": "433 Park Ave, New York",     "iata_code": "",     "icao_code": "",     "lat": 40.7607634,     "lng": -73.971212,     "place_id": "EiU0MzMgUGFyayBBdmUsIE5ldyBZb3JrLCBOWSAxMDAyMiwgVVNB",     "timezone": "America/New_York"   } }` |

###  HOURLY SEARCHES {#hourly-searches}

**Endpoint**: `/v2/search/`  
**Allowed methods**: `POST`

**Highlights:**

* An hourly search works very similarly to a normal point to point search, except that you should pass us “hourly” for the value of the “mode” parameter, pass one additional parameter called “hourly\_booking\_duration” and no end\_location information should be included in the search.

| EXAMPLE: starting a search (note the empty `results` since polling is expected)  `POST /v2/search/ API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey> {   "start_address": "433 Park Ave, New York",   "mode": "hourly",   "hourly_booking_duration": 2,   "pickup_datetime": "2017-08-16 15:30",   "num_passengers": 2,   "currency": "USD" }` |
| :---- |
| `HTTP/1.1 201 Created {   "created_at": 1492730991,   "currency_info": {     "code": "USD",     "prefix_symbol": "$",     "suffix_symbol": ""   },   "expires_at": 1492731891,   "flight_datetime": null,   "flight_type": "domestic",   "more_coming": true,   "num_passengers": 2,   "pickup_datetime": "2017-08-16T15:30:00-04:00",   "results": [],   "search_id": "5c8563a5d31d4c33a3a1eafbbfe59c4b",   "start_location": {     "formatted_address": "433 Park Ave, New York, NY 10022, USA",     "full_address": "433 Park Ave, New York",     "iata_code": "",     "icao_code": "",     "lat": 40.7607634,     "lng": -73.971212,     "place_id": "EiU0MzMgUGFyayBBdmUsIE5ldyBZb3JrLCBOWSAxMDAyMiwgVVNB",     "timezone": "America/New_York"   } }` |

### POLLING FOR RESULTS

**Endpoint**: `/v2/search/<search_id>/poll/`  
**Allowed methods**: `GET`

**Highlights**:

* We recommend calling this endpoint approximately every 1-2 seconds for 10 seconds, although the vast majority of our search results will be available in 3-6 seconds. There is no point of polling for results every hundred milliseconds, as there will not be new results in such a small timeframe. It is the same for doing a poll request right after the search request, no results will be returned and everyone will just waste resources;  
* You should keep polling as long as the `more_coming` value is true. However, always set a timeout in your application to stop polling after a certain maximum amount of time, as in rare cases errors can cause the API to never return false. Normally, the maximum number of polls expected is 10\.  
* Every time you poll, `results` will contain different data. This is because our external providers’ APIs return data at a different pace. This also implies that polling results are not accumulable. We recommend returning these results to your customers as they appear and not waiting for everything to finish.  
* **Important:** Our API allows 30 poll requests for every search\_id per minute,, after that the request will be throttled. Our testing environment allows 10 poll requests for every search\_id, per minute.  
* In the poll response, you'll find detailed information about the products offered by different providers. Each product is identified by a result\_id. Certain providers require information about all passengers for whom a transfer is being booked. For instance, if the number of passengers is 2, you'll need to provide additional passenger information (extra\_pax\_info) when making a reservation. Failure to provide this information will result in a 400 error code, accompanied by the following message: {"non\_field\_errors":\[{"message":"Missing required argument extra\_pax\_info","code":"extra\_pax\_info\_required","user\_message":"Missing required argument extra\_pax\_info"}\]}  
* You can filter the results by amenities by passing the selected amenity as a parameter to this endpoint, e.g. if you want to receive in the response results from providers that have enabled ride-tracking, you’ll do it the following way: https://api.mozio.com/v2/search/8c0973af9d944917b05bd6bf1bcdc6a2/poll?amenities=ride\_tracking  
*  List of amenities can be found in the amenities section.

## **Vehicle Information in Search Results**

Each search result includes the following vehicle-related fields:

* `vehicle_class`

* `vehicle_type`

* `make`

* `model`

Please note that **only `vehicle_class` and `vehicle_type` are guaranteed**.

The `make` and `model` fields are provided for informational purposes only and **are not guaranteed**. We recommend displaying this information using phrasing such as *“this vehicle or similar”*.

Any alternative (similar) vehicle provided will always match the confirmed `vehicle_class` and `vehicle_type`.

| EXAMPLE: polling for search results using the `search_id` returned previously  `GET /v2/search/5c8563a5d31d4c33a3a1eafbbfe59c4b/poll/ API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey>` |

### 

### CANCELLATION POLICIES IN SEARCH RESULTS

During the search process, each result includes detailed cancellation policies to help users understand the conditions for cancelling a trip. The cancellation information is returned in the polling results under each result's main step.

The cancellation data is located in the cancellation dictionary under the policy key. This information includes:

* Notice: The number of hours before the ride can be canceled.  
* Refund Percent: The percentage of the refund that the passenger will receive if the ride is canceled (always 100%).

The JSONPath for accessing this information is:

$.results\[\*\].steps\[?(@.main \= true)\].details.cancellation.policy

For example:

| `{   "cancellation": {     "amendable": true,     "cancellable_offline": true,     "cancellable_online": true,     "policy": [       {         "notice": 24,         "refund_percent": 100       }     ]   } }`  |
| :---- |

This cancellation data is essential to display to users at the search stage to ensure they are aware of the terms before booking.

### STEP WALK IN THE SEARCH RESULTS 

In the response to the "Poll for Search Results" API, you will receive multiple results. Each result includes an ID and a steps field, which is a list of dictionaries.

Each dictionary in the steps list contains:

* A key named steps, indicating whether the step is a main one (e.g., related to a provider).  
* A key named step\_type, which specifies the type of step (e.g., bus, car, or walk).

If one of the steps has the type walk, it means the destination cannot be reached solely via a provider. Instead, the user will need to disembark at a location where the vehicle can stop and walk to the final destination.

TICKET TYPES & SCHEDULES

In the response from the Poll Search Results endpoint, some shared-ride services include a ticket\_types field. 

| EXAMPLE: updating a search (note the empty results since polling is expected)  GET /v2/search/d198708f579a42e49e49b94f5d79/poll/ /d API-KEY: \<myMozioAPIkey\>  |
| :---- |
| HTTP/1.1 200 OK "ticket\_types": \[   {     "ticket\_id": "2",     "ticket\_name": "Economy",     "count": 0,     "validity": "",     "default": true,     "default\_schedule\_index": 2,     "schedules": \[       {         "departure\_datetime": "2026-11-30T15:30:00Z",         "arrival\_datetime": "2026-11-30T16:28:42Z",         "duration": { "value": 3522 },         "transfers": 0,         "price": {           "value": "8.63",           "display": "US$8.63",           "compact": "US$8.63"         }       },       {         "departure\_datetime": "2026-11-30T16:00:00Z",         "arrival\_datetime": "2026-11-30T16:58:42Z",         "duration": { "value": 3522 },         "transfers": 1,         "price": {           "value": "17.24",           "display": "US$17.24",           "compact": "US$17"         }       }     \]   } \] |

### Booking Requirements

# When booking a ride with a provider that returns ticket\_types, the following rules apply:

#### 1\. Passenger Information

# You must provide extra\_pax\_info, as tickets are generated individually for each passenger.

#### 2\. Schedule-Based Tickets

# Tickets are generated for a specific departure time, defined by the schedules listed under the selected ticket type.

# By default, the system selects the schedule whose departure time is closest to the requested pickup datetime:

* # Pickup at 15:30 → ticket generated for 15:30 

* # Pickup at 15:40 → ticket generated for 15:30 

* # Pickup at 15:50 → ticket generated for 16:00 

# The schedule selected by default is indicated by the default\_schedule\_index field.  This index corresponds to the position of the schedule in the schedules array.

# Example: "default\_schedule\_index": 2

### Selecting a Different Schedule

You can override the default schedule by passing the alternative\_time\_index field in the reservation request.

Example:

| EXAMPLE: updating a search (note the empty results since polling is expected)  PATCH /v2/search/d198708f579a42e49e49b94f5d796c52/170da70e405c9c65979d8412b046ec9f/ac7410daf73e472f959e4eb3040e26f4/ /d API-KEY: \<myMozioAPIkey\> {   "search\_id": "c16263d8391b4138aff5e77b8ebba767",   "result\_id": "871ada97e91a208cb87f432f44abfe27",   "email": "email@mozio.com",   "phone\_number": "+483739229",   "first\_name": "JOSE MARIA",   "last\_name": "MARIA",   "airline": "LX",   "flight\_number": "8084",   "flight\_type": "international",   "alternative\_time\_index": 3 }  |
| :---- |
| HTTP/1.1 201 Created  |

# In this case, the ticket will be generated for the schedule at index 3 in the schedules list.

### Verifying the Generated Ticket Time

# You can confirm which schedule was applied by querying the Reservation Details endpoint:

# GET /v2/reservations/by\_search\_id/{search\_id}

# In the response, check the alternative\_time\_index field.

# This index refers to the alternative\_times list, and the corresponding time indicates the departure time for which the ticket is valid.

### UPDATING & REFRESHING A SEARCH {#updating-&-refreshing-a-search}

**Endpoint**: `/v2/search/<search_id>/<result_id>/`  
**Allowed methods**: `PATCH`

**Highlights**:

*  Use this endpoint to change search details(for example the pickup time or number of passengers) for a single quote that the customer is interested in booking  
* You can pass any search parameter to this method. This call returns a response in the exact same format as a new search, and just like a brand new search, it will require polling to get the data. However, this process is much faster than doing a new search since we will only be updating the single option.

| EXAMPLE: updating a search (note the empty `results` since polling is expected)  `PATCH /v2/search/d198708f579a42e49e49b94f5d796c52/170da70e405c9c65979d8412b046ec9f/ac7410daf73e472f959e4eb3040e26f4/` /d `API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey> {   "pickup_datetime": "2017-08-16 15:30",   "currency": "USD" }` |
| :---- |

# BOOKING

---

### STARTING THE PROCESS {#starting-the-process-1}

**Endpoint**: `/v2/reservations/`  
**Allowed methods**: `POST`

**Highlights**:

* As mentioned before, to create a reservation you will need both the `search_id` and `result_id` from the selected quote from the search process. Apart from that, most of the data required are contact details of the passenger(s).  
* The response from this endpoint will inform you about the status of the reservation you just tried to place; in most cases a successful response will be `pending`, meaning our API is contacting the external provider and waiting for a response. After this, you will need to start polling.  
* The response from this endpoint should be checked, i.e. it cannot be assumed that each time the response will be successful, sometimes the response will not be pending and that means that a reservation hasn’t been successfully created  
* Flight data (airline’s IATA code and flight number) is always required for a booking going to/from an airport, unless you are trying to book an express train or a public bus, in which case the search result will indicate flight data is not required. Specifically, you must provide the airline's IATA code \- it cannot be any other identifier of the airline, but the IATA code (e.g. “airline” \= “LX”) and the flight number (e.g. “flight\_number” \= “9202”. If you don’t provide flight details, we will return an error “invalid”, “Sorry, that airline is not in our database. Contact via chat and we'll try to help”  
* If you reservation is for a round-trip trip (`mode` \= `round_trip` when searching), don’t forget to provide `return_airline` and `return_flight_number`  
* No credit card data was needed because the integrating application is in charge of managing payment data  
* If you select a transfer option that requires extra passenger information (extra\_pax\_required \= True), please ensure to include this information in the reservation payload. If you don’t do so, you won’t be able to create a reservation and will receive a 400 error instead. Below is an example of such a payload for your reference.  
* Our API validates phone numbers using [Google’s libphonenumber library](https://github.com/google/libphonenumber), which follows official national numbering plans.  
* **Important**: Please send a reservation identifier from your side on the partner\_tracking\_id parameter in the payload for this endpoint, it will facilitate the reconciliation of bookings with finance teams.

**Duplicate reservation safety mechanism:**

1. **Same partner\_tracking\_id**  
    If multiple /v2/reservations requests are sent using the **same partner\_tracking\_id**, only the first reservation will be created. Subsequent requests with the same ID will be rejected as duplicates.

2. **Same search\_id**  
    If a reservation is created using a search\_id that has already been used for another reservation, it will be flagged as a duplicate.

3. **Matching Passenger & Trip Details**  
    If a new reservation request contains the exact same values for **all** of the following fields as an existing reservation:

   * first\_name

   * last\_name

   * airline

   * flight\_number

   * start\_address

   * end\_address

   * departure\_datetime

   * number\_of\_passengers

⚠️ **Tip:** To avoid duplicates, always generate unique partner\_tracking\_id values for each new reservation and ensure that repeated submissions (e.g., retries) are properly deduplicated on your side.

| EXAMPLE: creating a reservation using the sample result from the search polling response above  `POST /v2/reservations/ API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey> {   "search_id": "5c8563a5d31d4c33a3a1eafbbfe59c4b",   "result_id": "763475651c06f5ac31ea587084dc0629",   "email": "happytraveler@mozio.com",   "extra_pax_info": [        {           "first_name": "JOSE",          "last_name": "SMITH",        }     ],   "country_code_name": "US",   "phone_number": "+18775998200",   "first_name": "Happy",   "last_name": "Traveler",   "airline": "AA",   "flight_number": "123",   "customer_special_instructions": "My doorbell is broken, please yell",   “partner_tracking_id”: “1234567ABC” }` |
| :---- |
| `HTTP/1.1 201 Created {   "reservations": [],   "status": "pending" }` |

###  POLLING FOR RESULTS {#polling-for-results}

**Endpoint**: `/v2/reservations/<search_id>/poll/`  
**Allowed methods**: `GET`

**Highlights:**

* Reservations have one of 3 possible states: `pending` (the initial state, i.e. it’s been processed), `completed` (i.e. it was successful), `failed` (i.e. there was an error); we recommend you to poll each  every 1-2 seconds until the status of the reservations changes.  
* This method shall be called until the reservation has achieved either of the final states described above  
* If the method has got completed state, it’ll return details of the reservation for an hour from the time of making the reservation  
* To check the status of a reservation and/or retrieve details of the reservation, use a different endpoint (see [GETTING RESERVATION DETAILS](#getting-reservation-details---checking-reservation-status) )

| EXAMPLE: polling until the reservation is `completed` (with the `search_id` returned by the search process)  `GET /v2/reservations/5c8563a5d31d4c33a3a1eafbbfe59c4b/poll/ API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey>` |

# 

# RESERVATION CHANGES {#reservation-changes}

---

To make changes to a reservation, first we need to do a re-search passing the reservation id and the parameters we want to change, like a new start or end location, a pickup datetime etc.  
After this re-search is done, using the search\_id and result\_id a new reservation will be created using the reservation changes endpoint, passing again the old reservation id, this endpoint will return a new reservation, with new reservation id. The old reservation will be cancelled. That’s why only cancelable reservations can be changed. On a change, the price is subject to change and you should be sure to charge/refund your customer as needed.

The change process is meant to be a much simpler than doing a full search and booking because you only need to pass the information you want to change from an existing reservation, and the search will only return options from the same provider the original reservation was made with, making the search process much faster than a new search.

### Step 1 \- Doing the search changing parameters

**Endpoint**: `/v2/search/reservation_changes/`  
**Allowed methods**: `POST`

**Highlights**:

* The main idea behind changing a reservation is creating a new one with the requested changes, to do this we need to call first the re-search endpoint.  
* This endpoint is exactly the same as the normal search, with the difference that, we need to pass the reservation\_id and only pass the search params that we need to change.

| EXAMPLE: re-searching a created reservation with some differences  `POST /v2/search/reservation_changes/ API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey> {    "pickup_datetime": "2017-08-30 22:00",    "reservation_hashed_id": "5c8563a5d31d4c33a3a1eafbbfe59c4b" }`  |

### Step 2 \- Doing the reservation changing parameters

**Endpoint**: /v2/reservations/changes/  
**Allowed methods**: `POST`

**Highlights:**

* This part of the flow is where the new reservation is created, passing the `search_id` and `result_id` obtained in the re-search endpoint (above), also the id of the old reservation must be passed as the param *`old_reservation_id`.*  
* Any data not sent in the /v2/search/reservation\_changes/ call that needs to be updated can also be sent here, like the contact phone number, email, airline or flight number etc.  
* **Important**: To update \`phone\_number\`, in addition to a valid phone number, the field \`country\_code\_name\`  is required, other than that, the phone will not be updated.  
* `use_reservation_card` if set to True, the existing reservation payment method will be used in case the reservation price increased. This is also used by default if there is no change in the price.  
* After this method, the poll reservation endpoint must be called to get the final result, just like a normal reservation.  
* The new reservation ids should be used, and the old reservation will be cancelled.

| EXAMPLE: Creating changed reservation  `POST /v2/reservations/changes/ API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey> {   "old_reservation_id": "5c8563a5d31d4c33a3a1eafbbfe59c4b",   "search_id": "5c8563a5d31d4c33a3a1eafbbfe59c49",   "special_instructions": "Special instructions changed",   "result_id": "763475651c06f5ac31ea587084dc0640",   "email": "p.hamman@mozio.com",   "use_reservation_card": true,   “phone_number”: “+55999999999”,   “country_code_name” : “BR” }`  |
| :---- |
| `HTTP/1.1 201 Created {   "status": "pending",   "reservations": [] }`  |

# [AMENITIES](#amenities)  {#amenities}

---

* Upgrades to a trip that can be added to a trip, e.g. child seats, baby boosters, meet and greet  
* Available amenities vary depending on the provider and search parameters e.g. provider ***x*** may have available amenities on the day ***y*** but not on the day ***z***  
* By adding an amenity you only add 1 of each amenity  
* If you’d like to request more than one amenity, please use a customer\_special\_instructions field, with a message, e.g. “Please provide 2 child seats”.

### AVAILABLE AMENITIES:

"wifi":

* Provides wireless internet access to passengers during the trip.

"wheelchair":

* Accommodates passengers who use wheelchairs, ensuring accessibility and convenience.

"ride\_tracking":

* Allows passengers to track the status and location of their ride in real-time.

"live\_tracking":

* Offers live tracking of the vehicle's location, enabling passengers to see the vehicle's current position on a map.

"provider\_driver\_information":

* Shares information about the driver, such as name, contact details, and profile, for passenger security and comfort.

"baby\_seats":

* Provides seats specifically designed for infants, ensuring their safety during the trip.

"child\_booster":

* Provides booster seats for young children to ensure their safety and comfort.

"pets":

* Allows passengers to bring their pets along for the ride.

"meet\_and\_greet":

* Offers a meet-and-greet service where the driver meets the passenger at a designated location, typically at airports or stations.

"english":

* Ensures that the driver or service provider speaks English, facilitating better communication.

"power":

* Offers access to power outlets or USB ports for charging electronic devices during the trip.

"extra\_waiting\_time\_thirty\_min":

* Up to 30 minutes of extra waiting time included.

"extra\_waiting\_time\_sixty\_min":

* Up to 60 minutes of extra waiting time included.

## **Internal Amenities**

### **`sms_notifications`**

`sms_notifications` is an internal amenity that is available for **all rides**, regardless of whether the transportation provider explicitly offers it.

* **Price:** 1.99 USD (applied only if selected)

* **Availability:** Always available

* **Behavior:**

  * If this amenity is selected **and** the provider offers either:

    * `ride_tracking`, or

    * `provider_driver_information`  
       (these amenities will appear in the provider’s amenities list),

  * the customer will receive an SMS notification when the driver has been assigned.

> If neither `ride_tracking` nor `provider_driver_information` is available for the selected provider, the SMS notification will not be sent even if `sms_notifications` is selected.

### RETRIEVING A LIST OF AMENITIES 

**Endpoint**: `/v2/amenities/`  
**Allowed methods**: `GET`

| EXAMPLE: sending an API request and receiving a response with a list of amenities  `GET /v2/amenities/ API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey>` |
| :---- |
| `HTTP/1.1 200 OK [   {    "amenity_id": "baby_seats",    "description": "Your vehicle will have a child safety seat to keep children under     age 4 safe.",    "display_name": "Baby seats",    "image_url": "https://static.mozio.com/amenities/baby-seats.svg",    "png_image_url": "https://static.mozio.com/amenities/baby-seats.png" }, … ]`  |

**Highlights:** 

* This endpoint shows amenities available on Mozio API  
* Amenities that each provider offers can be accessed through the search results after calling a search result poll method

| EXAMPLE: sending an API request and receiving a response from a search result \- the pasted reply shows a part of a response showing available amenities from a provider  `GET /v2/search/<search_id>/poll/ API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey>` |
| :---- |
| `HTTP/1.1 200 OK …  "wait_time": {  "minutes_included": 15,  "waiting_minute_price": null },  "amenities": [    {      "key": "baby_seats",      "name": "Baby seats",       "description": "Your vehicle will have a child safety seat to keep children  under age 4 safe.",      "image_url": "https://static.mozio.com/amenities/baby-seats.svg",      "png_image_url": "https://static.mozio.com/amenities/baby-seats.png",      "input_type": "numeric",      "included": false,      "selected": false,      "price": {        "value": "4.00",         "display": "$4.00",        "compact": "$4.00"       }   },   {      "key": "child_booster",      "name": "Child booster",      "description": "Your vehicle will have a child booster seat to keep children from age 4-8 safe.",      "image_url": "https://static.mozio.com/amenities/baby-seats.svg",      "png_image_url": "https://static.mozio.com/amenities/baby-seats.png",      "input_type": "numeric",      "included": false,      "selected": false,      "price": {       "value": "4.00",       "display": "$4.00",       "compact": "$4.00"      }   } … ]`  |

### RETRIEVING TOTAL COST OF A TRIP (WITH AMENITIES)

**Endpoint**: /v2/pricing/  
**Allowed methods**: POST, GET

**Highlights**

- To add an amenity to a trip, result\_id, search id and a list of amenities’ keys need to be provided as data or query parameters    
- If adding amenity as a query parameter, values must be provided as a key=value pair for each list member. For example, ?amenities=wifi\&amenities=child\_booster will be treated as \["wifi", "child\_booster"\].  
- The endpoint returns a total cost of a trip with selected amenities  
- Both GET and POST methods can be used to retrieve a total cost of a trip (inclusive of amenities)

| EXAMPLE: retrieving a total price of a booking inclusive of amenities: baby\_seats, child\_booster  `POST /v2/pricing/ API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey> {   "search_id": "73a5670b476649a985f0535db1077c05",   "result_id": "fe94b51ccd0623a9f1adabfbe0614d34",   "optional_amenities":["baby_seats", "child_booster"] }`  |
| :---- |
| `HTTP/1.1 200 OK {   "key": "baby_seats",   "name": "Baby seats",   "description": "Your vehicle will have a child safety seat to keep children under age 4 safe.",  "image_url": "https://static.mozio.com/amenities/baby-seats.svg",  "png_image_url": "https://static.mozio.com/amenities/baby-seats.png",  "input_type": "numeric",  "included": false,  "selected": true,  "price": {  "value": "4.00",  "display": "$4.00",  "compact": "$4.00" } }, {  "key": "child_booster",  "name": "Child booster",  "description": "Your vehicle will have a child booster seat to keep children from   age 4-8 safe.",  "image_url": "https://static.mozio.com/amenities/baby-seats.svg",  "png_image_url": "https://static.mozio.com/amenities/baby-seats.png",  "input_type": "numeric",  "included": false,  "selected": true,  "price": {  "value": "4.00",  "display": "$4.00",  "compact": "$4.00" } }  "final_price": {  "value": "178.40",  "display": "$178.40",  "compact": "$178",  "currency": "USD",  "smallest_currency_unit": 17840 },`  |

# [GRATUITY](#gratuity) {#gratuity}

---

Adding Gratuity to a Reservation

To add gratuity to a reservation, include one of the following fields in the reservation creation request body:

* gratuity\_percent — an integer representing a percentage (e.g. 15 for 15%)  
* gratuity\_amount — a flat monetary value

Use only one of the two fields. If both are provided, gratuity\_amount takes precedence.

Gratuity is not applied automatically and is not a persistent account-level setting. It must be specified on each individual reservation request where it should apply.

Once a reservation has been created, its gratuity value cannot be modified afterward, so the correct amount must be included at the time of booking.

Gratuity support can also vary by provider. Some providers already include gratuity within their quoted price, and a small number of providers do not support added gratuity at all — in either case, these fields will have no additional effect on that particular booking.  
In the search poll response, whether gratuity is already reflected in a result's price can be checked in the price object of each result step — the gratuity field there shows the gratuity amount currently factored into that quoted price.

# AIRLINES AND FLIGHTS VERIFICATION 

---

### VERIFY FLIGHTS

**Endpoint**: `/v2/flights/verify/`  
**Allowed methods**: `POST`

| EXAMPLE: retrieving flight information  `POST /v2/flights/verify API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey> {     "return_voyage": true,     "pickup_datetime": "2024-06-26T08:00:00+07:00",     "airline_code": "5J",     "airport_code": "BKK",     "flight_direction": "dep",     "flight_number": "930",     "search_id": "7814f4dde857468dadb5d0f964237525" }`  |
| :---- |
| `HTTP/1.1 200 OK {     "is_valid": false,     "message_title": "Late Arrival!",     "message": "You're expected to arrive at the airport at <b>9:30AM</b>.<br/>This gives you 1 hours and 45 minutes until your flight.<br/>To ensure you don't miss it, we recommend arriving 3 hours before departure.",     "extra_data": {         "possible_pickup_datetime": "2024-06-26T06:45:00+07:00"     } }`  |

**Highlights:** 

* The endpoint allows you to verify if the selected pick-up time is suitable or if opting for an earlier time would be more convenient.  
* This endpoint lets you confirm if there's a suitable flight match found for the details of your reservation

### Check Flights

* You can pass different parameters and retrieve details of your flight. 

**Endpoint**: `/v2/flights/?airline_code=<airline_code>&airport_code=<airport_code>&flight_direction=<flight_direction>&pickup_datetime=<pickup_datetime>&flight_number=<flight_number>`  
**Allowed methods**: `GET`

| EXAMPLE: retrieving details of a flight  `GET /v2/flights/?airline_code=W6&airport_code=BCN&flight_direction=arriving&pickup_datetime=2024-06-30T10%3A45&flight_number=1705`  |
| :---- |
| `HTTP/1.1 200 OK {     "flights": [         {             "airline": {                 "airline_code": "W6",                 "airline_name": "Wizz Air"             },             "flight_number": "1705",             "flight_code": "W61705",             "flight_type": "international",             "origin": "GDN",             "destination": "BCN",             "origin_terminal": null,             "destination_terminal": null,             "time": "9:10PM",             "datetime": "2024-06-30T21:10:00+02:00"         }     ] }`  |

# RETRIEVING DRIVERS’ DETAILS

---

### CHECK DRIVERS’ DETAILS

**Endpoint**: `/v2/reservations/{hashed_id}/vehicle/`  
**Allowed methods**: `GET`

| EXAMPLE: retrieving vehicle information  `GET /v2/reservations/1231231241fdasfaa/vehicle/ API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey>`  |
| :---- |
| `HTTP/1.1 200 OK {   "status": "active",   "driver": {     "id": 123,     "external_id": "DRV456",     "name": "John Doe",     "phone": "+1234567890",     "license_number": "AB123456",     "image_url": "http://example.com/driver123.jpg"   },   "vehicle": {     "id": 789,     "external_id": "VEH789",     "vehicle_type": "Sedan",     "manufacturer": "Toyota",     "model": "Camry",     "plate": "XYZ1234",     "color": "Blue",     "description": "A blue Toyota Camry in excellent condition.",     "image_url": "http://example.com/vehicle789.jpg"   } }`  |

**Highlights:** 

* **Verify Driver Information**: The endpoint allows you to verify the driver's details, including their name, phone number, license number, and profile image. This helps ensure you have accurate and up-to-date information about the driver assigned to your trip.  
* **Check Vehicle Details:** This endpoint lets you confirm the details of the assigned vehicle, such as the vehicle type, manufacturer, model, plate number, color, and a description along with an image. This ensures you know exactly what vehicle to expect for your journey.

### CHECK DRIVERS POSITION

**Endpoint**: `/v1/tracking/{hashed_id}/events/latest`  
**Allowed methods**: `GET`

| EXAMPLE: retrieving driver’s position  `GET /v1/tracking/1231231241fdasfaa/events/latest API-KEY: <myMozioAPIkey>`  |
| :---- |
| `HTTP/1.1 200 OK {     "lat": 30.0,     "lng": 30.0,     "status": "driver_departed_to_pickup",     "timestamp": "2024-07-25T17:47:01.761854Z",     "tracking_id": "c90n51960f274447b29473fc0d995f6a" }`  |

**Highlights:** 

* This endpoint can be called multiple times to reflect the current status of the driver, as well as their latitude (`lat`) and longitude (`lng`).  
* **Available statuses include:**  "cancelled", "not\_started", "driver\_departed\_to\_pickup", "driver\_arrived\_at\_pickup", "driver\_departed\_to\_dropoff",  "driver\_arrived\_at\_dropoff", "no\_show\_reported\_by\_driver"   
* Timestamp refers to the time at which the latest data was obtained from




### 

### **ERROR CODES**

#### GENERAL

**ServerError**  
    error\_code \= "server\_error"

   *It’s raised when the server encounters an unexpected condition*

#### AUTHORIZATION

**MissingApiKey**  
    error\_code \= "required\_api\_key"

   *It’s raised when the user doesn’t provide an API key in the request*

**InvalidApiKeyException**  
    error\_code \= "invalid\_api\_key"

   *It’s raised when the user provides a wrong API key*

#### RESERVATION CANCELLATION 

**AlreadyCancelledException**  
    error\_code \= “res\_already\_canceled”

   *It’s raised when a user sends a request to cancel a reservation that is already canceled*

**TooLateToCancelException**  
    error\_code \= "too\_late\_to\_cancel"

   *It’s raised when a user sends a request to cancel a reservation that is not cancellable, i.e. cancellation policy doesn’t allow the cancellation*

**CancellationErrorException**  
    error\_code \= "server\_error"

   *It’s raised when there was an error in the reservation cancellation, it’s returned from the provider side*

#### RESERVATION CREATION

**DuplicateReservation**  
  error\_code \= "duplicate\_reservation"  
   
   *It’s raised when there is a request to create a reservation that we consider a duplicate reservation. A duplicate reservation is a reservation that matches  any of following criteria:*

***Reservation Status**: If the reservation is in a 'PENDING' or 'COMPLETED' state, it's considered a duplicate.*  
***Partner Tracking ID**: If there's a partner tracking ID and it hasn't been set to ignore partner tracking duplicate checks, and there exists a reservation with the same partner tracking ID that hasn't been canceled, it's considered a duplicate.*  
***Reservation Details**: If there's a reservation with matching details like the first name, last name, airline, flight number, start and end locations, departure datetime, and number of passengers, it's considered a duplicate.*

**TripPriceChanged**  
    error\_code \= "trip\_price\_changed"

   *It’s raised when the price has changed between doing a search a making a reservation request*

#### SEARCH

**SearchResultNotFound**  
    error\_code \= "search\_result\_not\_found"

   *It’s raised when the result\_id passed in the reservation create request can’t be found.* 

**SearchExpired**  
    error\_code \= "search\_expired"

   *It’s raised when the search has expired. We cache results for 20 minutes, after that time you need to refresh the search*

**429 Too Many Requests**  
    status\_code \= 429

   *It’s raised when a user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time (we have limits for search request and search poll requests: the limit is 100 search request and 30 search poll requests per search\_id per minute*

**400 Bad request**  
    error\_code \= “too\_far\_apart”

*It’s raised when doing a search request (or performing a search on Mozio website/white labels) and the distance between the from and to locations exceeds 500 miles.*
